items.title: Jason Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2025
items.q: He and Hank Jones, oh man, their playing’s just so fresh and his sound — so lyrical, his tone.

ctx.x: Um hum. Yeah, that version of “Cherokee” — when students want to learn “Cherokee” I’ll say you’ve got to learn it slow, listen to this, you know, and Joe Wilder’s playing is so angular, and it’s 1956 and it sounds like it could have been recorded, you know, yesterday. He and Hank Jones, oh man, their playing’s just so fresh and his sound — so lyrical, his tone. He could have played in any major orchestra.

Yeah. In fact, that was his aspiration when he — I got to know him fairly well and he wanted to be in a classical situation. And at the time there was no black players in — you know it was just not an opportunity that he could pursue. And you can hear that classical © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-
